1 أَثَلَ , aor.
اَثِلَ , inf. n. أُثُولٌ, It (anything, M) had, or came to have, root, or a foundation; or it was, or became, firm, or established, and firmly rooted or founded; as also ↓ تأثّل . (M, K.) ―
-b2- Also, inf. n. as above, It (dominion) was, or became, great; (TA;) and so ↓ the latter verb. (M, K. *) ―
-b3- And أَثُلَ, inf. n. أَثَالَةٌ, said of high rank, or nobility, It was, or became, old, of ancient origin, or of long standing. (TA.) ＝
-A2- See also 5.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
